To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.
6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external
email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each
(AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether
each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline view

The Seller says the package is "fair and balanced." It isn't. Taken together, the positions move almost all known risk onto Wattlebridge.

1. **Every identified problem is pushed into the general warranty regime.** That regime has a 20% cap, a deductible basket and an 18-month limit.
2. **The general regime is then neutralised** by general disclosure of the whole data room and public records, plus a constructive-knowledge exclusion. Read together, clauses 8.3 and Schedule 7 would leave the Buyer with very little recourse for any matter in the data room.
3. **The Seller's cover note contradicts its own Disclosure Letter on several points.** These are Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses and the incident. The Disclosure Letter is the more reliable document, and we should negotiate from it.

On the Disclosure Letter's own figures, quantifiable items not reflected in the Seller's price mechanics are at least:

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~AUD 3,200,000 |
| DD-005 bonuses (before on-costs) | AUD 420,000 |
| Ironquay SOW3 open | AUD 180,000 |
| Sandbar renewals (status unclear) | AUD 330,000 |
| **Total** | **~AUD 4.13m (~17% of price)** |

Bluefen revenue at risk (~30% of FY26 revenue) and the DD-006 privacy exposure come on top of this.

*Caveat: I have only the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA text or the underlying DD documents. Clause references follow the Seller's numbering. Points below should be checked against the full draft and DD-002 to DD-012 before the mark-up goes out.*

---

## Part A: Structural / limitation issues

### 1. Title and capacity warranties capped with general warranties (reject)
**Seller position:** Title and capacity warranties get the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity."

**Why it matters:** We are paying AUD 24m for the shares. If title fails, our loss is the whole price, and recovery would be capped at AUD 4.8m. This is not market practice.

**Push back:**
- Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, solvency, capital structure, no encumbrances over the shares) should be capped at 100% of the price.
- They should carry a long survival period, at least 6 years, consistent with NSW contract limitation periods. Use 12 years if the SPA is executed as a deed.
- They should sit outside the de minimis and basket.

**Title evidence is thin.** DD-012 is only the Company's own register, and Disclosure Letter item 10 expressly disclaims any statement that title has been verified. We should require:
- an ASIC company extract reconciled to the register;
- the share certificates, or evidence the shares are uncertificated;
- the issue history, showing all shares fully paid;
- PPSR searches against both Harbourglass and Paperbark;
- confirmation that Riverlark holds no security over the shares themselves, such as a share mortgage or a general security agreement over the Seller.

### 2. "Limitations apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 and cl 12.3/13 default rule) (reject)
**Seller position:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply universally. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

**Why it matters:** This silently caps and time-bars:
- specific indemnities;
- tax;
- breach of covenants (including pre-Completion conduct and restraints);
- price adjustment and leakage claims;
- potentially fraud.

**Push back:**
- **Reverse the default rule.** Limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.
- **Express carve-outs** from all limitations for:
  - fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by the Seller, the Company or their representatives;
  - fundamental warranties;
  - the tax indemnity;
  - specific indemnities;
  - covenant breaches;
  - price adjustment and completion accounts mechanics.
- **Non-reliance:** keep it narrow. It must not exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct where the law does not permit that, and it must not apply to the Warranties or the Disclosure Letter.

### 3. Cap, thresholds and time limits (cl 12.1–12.3)
- **Cap at 20% (AUD 4.8m):** This is within the market range for general warranties, and could be acceptable *if* the carve-outs above are agreed. Link it to the W&I strategy, if we are using W&I.
- **De minimis AUD 25,000:** Seek AUD 10,000. Related or recurring claims arising from the same facts must aggregate. Otherwise the three Sandbar renewals, or many individual privacy claims, could each fall below the threshold.
- **Basket AUD 250,000, excess only:** Seek a **tipping basket** so that, once exceeded, recovery runs from the first dollar. Seek a lower figure (~0.5%, AUD 120,000).
- **18 months:** Seek 24 months, so that at least one full audit cycle is covered.
  - Tax: 5–7 years, or the relevant ATO amendment period plus 6 months.
  - Fundamentals: as above.

### 4. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" (reject)
- **Tax:** We need a standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes. It should sit outside the cap, basket and knowledge or disclosure qualifiers. Payroll tax and superannuation on the DD-005 bonuses (item 9 below) should be covered expressly.
- **IP:** Given Ironquay (item 8 below), we should not accept that IP warranties are purely general. At a minimum, the IP ownership warranty should be treated as a fundamental-lite warranty with a higher cap and longer survival, alongside a specific indemnity.

### 5. General disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2) (reject)
**Seller position:** Everything in the data room as at 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records, is disclosed against all warranties.

**Push back:**
- Strike general disclosure of the data room and public registers. At most, allow general disclosure of searches the Buyer actually conducted, on specified dates.
- Only matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter should qualify the warranties. "Fairly disclosed" should mean disclosed with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and financial effect of the matter.
- Disclosure must not qualify:
  - fundamental warranties;
  - the tax indemnity;
  - specific indemnities.

**Staleness:** The letter speaks at 22 September 2026, and it is now 6 November 2026. We should require:
- an updated disclosure as at signing;
- warranties repeated at Completion;
- no right for the Seller to disclose against the repeated warranties. Alternatively, any new disclosure should give the Buyer a termination right and preserve its claims.

**Item 1.4 (non-admission):** This is tolerable in principle. Make clear it does not reduce the effect of the specific disclosures, and that the specific disclosures are themselves warranted as true, complete and not misleading.

### 6. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3) (reject)
**Seller position:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

**Why it matters:** This is anti-sandbagging based on *constructive* knowledge, attributed through every adviser. Combined with general disclosure, it guts the warranties. It could also be argued to defeat the specific indemnities we need, because the indemnified matters are by definition known.

**Push back:**
- Delete it. Replace it with an express statement that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed.
- **Fallback:** limit the exclusion to the actual knowledge of named individuals of facts they knew constituted a breach. Specific indemnities, tax and fundamentals should sit outside it entirely.

---

## Part B: Specific matters

### 7. Bluefen change-of-control consent (cl 3 / 6.3) (critical)
**Facts (Disclosure Letter item 2):**
- Bluefen accounts for ~AUD 3.6m, or ~30%, of FY26 revenue.
- The contract has a change-control consent requirement (cl 11.2), with conditions attached (cl 11.3).
- The Seller has **not** provided a final written consent, or any evidence that the conditions are met.

**Mismatch:** The cover note says the consent "is addressed." It plainly is not.

**Problems with the Seller's mechanism:**
- "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak obligation.
- Treating the condition as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" would let a *conditional* or adverse consent count as satisfied. That would leave the cl 11.3 conditions unresolved, or require changes to the contract terms.

**Push back:**
- The condition precedent should require **unconditional written consent from Bluefen, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably)**.
- The cl 11.3 conditions must be satisfied, or waived by Bluefen, with no adverse amendment to the contract's term, pricing, termination rights or exclusivity.
- The Seller should use **all reasonable endeavours** or best endeavours. The Buyer should approve communications with Bluefen and be able to participate in them.
- Only the Buyer may waive the condition.
- There should be a sunset date, with a Buyer walk right if it is not met.
- Add a warranty that Bluefen has not given notice of termination, non-renewal or a material reduction in volume. Consider a material adverse change (MAC) right, or a price adjustment or earn-out, if Bluefen is lost or its revenue reduced within a defined period.

### 8. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) (critical)
**Facts (Disclosure Letter item 3):**
- ~AUD 3.2m is outstanding.
- The facility has change-control (cl 8.1) and discharge (cl 9.2) provisions.
- It has not been repaid, and there is no discharge of security.

**Problem:** The Seller proposes a release "following Completion." This deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release means:
- we would own a company whose facility may be in default, or accelerable, on Completion under cl 8.1;
- the Company's assets would remain encumbered.

**Push back:**
- The facility should be repaid **at Completion out of the purchase price**, under a payoff letter from Riverlark that sets out the exact payout figure and daily interest.
- Riverlark should deliver, **as Completion deliverables**:
  - a deed of release covering all security;
  - signed PPSR financing change statements, or an undertaking to lodge them within 1 business day;
  - releases of any real property security;
  - releases of guarantees given by the Company.
- All facility debt, including accrued interest, break costs and fees, should be counted as **Debt** and deducted from the price.
- If Riverlark has any security over the Seller's shares, its release goes to title (item 1).

### 9. DD-005 Completion bonuses: AUD 420,000 (high)
**Facts (Disclosure Letter item 5):**
- There are conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000.
- They are **not in the funds flow**.
- On-costs are not addressed.

**Problem:** The cover note says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller." But the employing entity is Paperbark. If they are not itemised and deducted, the Company, and therefore the Buyer, pays them after Completion.

**On-costs that are likely to apply:**
- NSW payroll tax;
- PAYG withholding;
- potentially superannuation guarantee. The ATO generally treats retention and completion-type bonuses as ordinary time earnings.
- workers' compensation premium impacts.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses and all associated on-costs as **Transaction Costs / Debt-like items** and deduct them from the price.
- Alternatively, have the Seller fund them at Completion, paid through Company payroll so that PAYG is withheld.
- Add an uncapped specific indemnity for any shortfall. It should cover any claim by employees who argue that the continued-employment conditions were met or waived.
- Obtain the bonus letters (DD-005) to confirm the conditions, the timing, and whether any part is payable after Completion.

### 10. Ironquay SOW3 IP (cl 11.1) (high)
**Facts (Disclosure Letter item 4):**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open.
- There is no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment.

**Problem:** The Company may not own the SOW3 materials. The Seller's indemnity covers only the payment itself. It does not cover:
- loss of the IP;
- infringement claims by Ironquay;
- the cost of re-engineering;
- customer claims if delivered products incorporate the materials.

**Push back:**
- Make it a condition or Completion deliverable that the Company provides **evidence of cleared payment** of all SOW3 fees and a **signed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay**. Ironquay should also confirm that no amounts remain owing.
- If the 180,000 remains unpaid, treat it as Debt and deduct it from the price.
- **Broaden cl 11.1** to cover all Losses arising from the Company not owning, or not being free to use, the SOW3 materials, and from any Ironquay claim. The indemnity should be outside the cap, basket and knowledge or disclosure exclusions, with survival of at least 6 years.
- Consider a specific escrow amount until the assignment is delivered.

### 11. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6) (high)
**Facts (Disclosure Letter item 6):**
- A download link was sent to an unintended external email address.
- The export may contain ~1,240 records of personal information.
- Access, scope and whether notification is required are all unknown.
- The investigation is preliminary.

**Problem:** The cover note calls the matter "not expected to be material." The Seller's own disclosure does not support that statement. There are several live risks:
- **Notifiable Data Breaches scheme:** under the Privacy Act, an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days. That period has very likely run since 22 September. A failure to assess or notify is itself a compliance issue.
- **Expanded penalty and enforcement regime:** the Privacy Act regime has been strengthened.
- **New statutory tort:** a statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy now applies.
- **Customer contract exposure:** this includes potential exposure under the Bluefen contract.

**Push back:**
- **Information rights now:** the incident date, the forensic report, access logs, and the Company's documented eligible data breach assessment. If the OAIC or individuals were notified, we need copies of those notifications.
- **Pre-Completion covenant:** the Company must complete the investigation and make any required notifications, in consultation with the Buyer.
- **Specific indemnity** for all Losses arising from the incident, including:
  - regulator costs and penalties, where they are lawfully indemnifiable;
  - claims by individuals;
  - customer claims and credits;
  - remediation costs.
  The indemnity should be outside the cap, basket and knowledge or disclosure exclusions, with survival of at least 3–4 years, and supported by escrow.
- **Warranties:** privacy and data security compliance, and no other incidents.
- **Insurance:** check whether the incident has been notified to the Company's cyber insurer, and if not, require it.
- **Delete** any characterisation of the matter as "not material" from the SPA and schedules.

### 12. Sandbar supplier renewals: 3 × AUD 110,000 (medium–high)
**Facts (Disclosure Letter item 8):**
- There are three "related" renewals totalling AUD 330,000.
- The Seller's own disclosure says to "read together for timing/scope."
- It is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Concern:** The pattern suggests a single commitment split into three parts, possibly to sit under:
- an approval threshold in the conduct-of-business covenants;
- a delegated authority limit;
- the de minimis.
The word "related" also raises a possible related-party question.

**Push back:**
- **Obtain the contracts (DD-008, DD-011)** and establish:
  - signing dates, and whether they were signed in the interim period;
  - the counterparty's identity and any relationship to Harbourglass;
  - term, termination rights and prepayment;
  - whether the value is accrued in the accounts.
- If the renewals are not ordinary course, require the Seller to either:
  - procure their termination or reduction pre-Completion; or
  - bear them through a price deduction or specific indemnity.
- Aggregation language in the de minimis (item 3) should capture series contracts.
- The conduct-of-business covenants should aggregate related or series contracts for the purpose of approval thresholds.

### 13. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) (medium)
The Seller's characterisations ("not a consent requirement"; "not triggered by share sale") are **not** warranted, and should not be relied on without our own review.

- **Lease:** Review DD-007 ourselves for deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording. Make the landlord notification a Completion deliverable, or a covenant with evidence of delivery. Add a warranty that no landlord consent is required.
- **Mossvale:** Check DD-009 for any definition of "assignment" that captures a change in control or a change in beneficial ownership. If it is ambiguous, seek a comfort or waiver letter pre-Completion.

---

## Part C: Security for claims

Harbourglass is a venture vehicle, so it may distribute the sale proceeds quickly. Even good contractual rights may then be hard to enforce. We should seek:
- **a general escrow or retention** of ~10% of the price for the general warranty survival period;
- **specific escrows** for:
  - Ironquay, until the assignment is delivered;
  - DD-006, until the investigation closes and the notification position is settled;
  - Bluefen, if Completion proceeds without full comfort.
- **a parent or fund guarantee**, if the escrow is not agreed.

**W&I note:** If W&I insurance is contemplated, known matters (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar) will be excluded from cover. They therefore need Seller-backed specific indemnities and escrow regardless.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Title/capacity | Same cap and time as general | 100% cap, 6+ yrs (12 if deed), outside thresholds; independent title verification | Critical |
| 2 | Limitations scope | Apply to all Claims | Apply to general warranties only; carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, indemnities, covenants, price mechanics | Critical |
| 3 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; any written consent suffices | Condition precedent: unconditional consent satisfactory to Buyer, 11.3 conditions met, Buyer-only waiver, sunset and walk right | Critical |
| 4 | Riverlark (~3.2m) | Release after Completion | Payoff at Completion from price; deed of release and PPSR releases as Completion deliverables; treat as Debt | Critical |
| 5 | General disclosure | Whole data room and public records | Specific, fair disclosure only; updated as at signing; no disclosure against repeated warranties | High |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Constructive knowledge bars claims | Delete; fallback to actual knowledge of named people; never affects indemnities | High |
| 7 | Bonuses (420k + on-costs) | "Matter for Seller," not in funds flow | Deduct as Transaction Costs incl. payroll tax and super; pay via payroll; indemnity | High |
| 8 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Payment evidence and confirmatory assignment at Completion; broad uncapped IP indemnity; escrow | High |
| 9 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Full information now; NDB compliance covenant; uncapped specific indemnity; escrow; delete characterisation | High |
| 10 | Tax/IP regime | General regime | Standalone tax indemnity (5–7 yrs, uncapped); IP ownership as fundamental-lite | High |
| 11 | Cap/thresholds/time | 20% / 25k / 250k deductible / 18 m | 20% acceptable with carve-outs; 10k de minimis with aggregation; tipping basket ~120k; 24 months | Medium |
| 12 | Sandbar (330k) | Ordinary course | Diligence the contracts; aggregate series contracts; terminate or deduct/indemnify if not ordinary course | Medium–High |
| 13 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed (unwarranted) | Our own review; warranties; notice or comfort letters as Completion deliverables | Medium |
| 14 | Security | None offered | ~10% general escrow plus specific escrows or guarantee | High |
| 15 | Stale disclosure | As at 22 Sep 2026 | Bring-down to signing and Completion; Buyer termination right for new matters | Medium |

**Immediate next steps:**
1. Send an information request covering:
   - the Bluefen correspondence;
   - the Riverlark payout letter;
   - Ironquay payment evidence;
   - the DD-006 forensic report and eligible data breach assessment;
   - the Sandbar contracts and their counterparty's identity;
   - the DD-005 bonus letters;
   - an ASIC extract and PPSR searches.
2. Prepare the SPA mark-up on the positions above.
3. Update the price and funds-flow model to show the ~AUD 4.13m of debt-like and price-relevant items.
4. Confirm the W&I approach, since it determines how much of the above must be Seller-backed.

  - covenant breaches;
  - price adjustment and completion accounts mechanics.
- **Non-reliance:** keep it narrow. It must not exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct where the law does not permit that, and it must not apply to the Warranties or the Disclosure Letter.

### 3. Cap, thresholds and time limits (cl 12.1–12.3)
- **Cap at 20% (AUD 4.8m):** This is within the market range for general warranties, and could be acceptable *if* the carve-outs above are agreed. Link it to the W&I strategy, if we are using W&I.
- **De minimis AUD 25,000:** Seek AUD 10,000. Related or recurring claims arising from the same facts must aggregate. Otherwise the three Sandbar renewals, or many individual privacy claims, could each fall below the threshold.
- **Basket AUD 250,000, excess only:** Seek a **tipping basket** so that, once exceeded, recovery runs from the first dollar. Seek a lower figure (~0.5%, AUD 120,000).
- **18 months:** Seek 24 months, so that at least one full audit cycle is covered.
  - Tax: 5–7 years, or the relevant ATO amendment period plus 6 months.
  - Fundamentals: as above.

### 4. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" (reject)
- **Tax:** We need a standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes. It should sit outside the cap, basket and knowledge or disclosure qualifiers. Payroll tax and superannuation on the DD-005 bonuses (item 9 below) should be covered expressly.
- **IP:** Given Ironquay (item 8 below), we should not accept that IP warranties are purely general. At a minimum, the IP ownership warranty should be treated as a fundamental-lite warranty with a higher cap and longer survival, alongside a specific indemnity.

### 5. General disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2) (reject)
**Seller position:** Everything in the data room as at 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records, is disclosed against all warranties.

**Push back:**
- Strike general disclosure of the data room and public registers. At most, allow general disclosure of searches the Buyer actually conducted, on specified dates.
- Only matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter should qualify the warranties. "Fairly disclosed" should mean disclosed with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and financial effect of the matter.
- Disclosure must not qualify:
  - fundamental warranties;
  - the tax indemnity;
  - specific indemnities.

**Staleness:** The letter speaks at 22 September 2026, and it is now 6 November 2026. We should require:
- an updated disclosure as at signing;
- warranties repeated at Completion;
- no right for the Seller to disclose against the repeated warranties. Alternatively, any new disclosure should give the Buyer a termination right and preserve its claims.

**Item 1.4 (non-admission):** This is tolerable in principle. Make clear it does not reduce the effect of the specific disclosures, and that the specific disclosures are themselves warranted as true, complete and not misleading.

### 6. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3) (reject)
**Seller position:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

**Why it matters:** This is anti-sandbagging based on *constructive* knowledge, attributed through every adviser. Combined with general disclosure, it guts the warranties. It could also be argued to defeat the specific indemnities we need, because the indemnified matters are by definition known.

**Push back:**
- Delete it. Replace it with an express statement that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed.
- **Fallback:** limit the exclusion to the actual knowledge of named individuals of facts they knew constituted a breach. Specific indemnities, tax and fundamentals should sit outside it entirely.

## Part B: Specific matters

### 7. Bluefen change-of-control consent (cl 3 / 6.3) (critical)
**Facts (Disclosure Letter item 2):**
- Bluefen accounts for ~AUD 3.6m, or ~30%, of FY26 revenue.
- The contract has a change-control consent requirement (cl 11.2), with conditions attached (cl 11.3).
- The Seller has **not** provided a final written consent, or any evidence that the conditions are met.

**Mismatch:** The cover note says the consent "is addressed." It plainly is not.

**Problems with the Seller's mechanism:**
- "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak obligation.
- Treating the condition as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" would let a *conditional* or adverse consent count as satisfied. That would leave the cl 11.3 conditions unresolved, or require changes to the contract terms.

**Push back:**
- The condition precedent should require **unconditional written consent from Bluefen, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably)**.
- The cl 11.3 conditions must be satisfied, or waived by Bluefen, with no adverse amendment to the contract's term, pricing, termination rights or exclusivity.
- The Seller should use **all reasonable endeavours** or best endeavours. The Buyer should approve communications with Bluefen and be able to participate in them.
- Only the Buyer may waive the condition.
- There should be a sunset date, with a Buyer walk right if it is not met.
- Add a warranty that Bluefen has not given notice of termination, non-renewal or a material reduction in volume. Consider a material adverse change (MAC) right, or a price adjustment or earn-out, if Bluefen is lost or its revenue reduced within a defined period.

### 8. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) (critical)
**Facts (Disclosure Letter item 3):**
- ~AUD 3.2m is outstanding.
- The facility has change-control (cl 8.1) and discharge (cl 9.2) provisions.
- It has not been repaid, and there is no discharge of security.

**Problem:** The Seller proposes a release "following Completion." This deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release means:
- we would own a company whose facility may be in default, or accelerable, on Completion under cl 8.1;
- the Company's assets would remain encumbered.

**Push back:**
- The facility should be repaid **at Completion out of the purchase price**, under a payoff letter from Riverlark that sets out the exact payout figure and daily interest.
- Riverlark should deliver, **as Completion deliverables**:
  - a deed of release covering all security;
  - signed PPSR financing change statements, or an undertaking to lodge them within 1 business day;
  - releases of any real property security;
  - releases of guarantees given by the Company.
- All facility debt, including accrued interest, break costs and fees, should be counted as **Debt** and deducted from the price.
- If Riverlark has any security over the Seller's shares, its release goes to title (item 1).

### 9. DD-005 Completion bonuses: AUD 420,000 (high)
**Facts (Disclosure Letter item 5):**
- There are conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000.
- They are **not in the funds flow**.
- On-costs are not addressed.

**Problem:** The cover note says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller." But the employing entity is Paperbark. If they are not itemised and deducted, the Company, and therefore the Buyer, pays them after Completion.

**On-costs that are likely to apply:**
- NSW payroll tax;
- PAYG withholding;
- potentially superannuation guarantee. The ATO generally treats retention and completion-type bonuses as ordinary time earnings.
- workers' compensation premium impacts.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses and all associated on-costs as **Transaction Costs / Debt-like items** and deduct them from the price.
- Alternatively, have the Seller fund them at Completion, paid through Company payroll so that PAYG is withheld.
- Add an uncapped specific indemnity for any shortfall. It should cover any claim by employees who argue that the continued-employment conditions were met or waived.
- Obtain the bonus letters (DD-005) to confirm the conditions, the timing, and whether any part is payable after Completion.

### 10. Ironquay SOW3 IP (cl 11.1) (high)
**Facts (Disclosure Letter item 4):**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open.
- There is no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment.

**Problem:** The Company may not own the SOW3 materials. The Seller's indemnity covers only the payment itself. It does not cover:
- loss of the IP;
- infringement claims by Ironquay;
- the cost of re-engineering;
- customer claims if delivered products incorporate the materials.

**Push back:**
- Make it a condition or Completion deliverable that the Company provides **evidence of cleared payment** of all SOW3 fees and a **signed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay**. Ironquay should also confirm that no amounts remain owing.
- If the 180,000 remains unpaid, treat it as Debt and deduct it from the price.
- **Broaden cl 11.1** to cover all Losses arising from the Company not owning, or not being free to use, the SOW3 materials, and from any Ironquay claim. The indemnity should be outside the cap, basket and knowledge or disclosure exclusions, with survival of at least 6 years.
- Consider a specific escrow amount until the assignment is delivered.

### 11. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6) (high)
**Facts (Disclosure Letter item 6):**
- A download link was sent to an unintended external email address.
- The export may contain ~1,240 records of personal information.
- Access, scope and whether notification is required are all unknown.
- The investigation is preliminary.

**Problem:** The cover note calls the matter "not expected to be material." The Seller's own disclosure does not support that statement. There are several live risks:
- **Notifiable Data Breaches scheme:** under the Privacy Act, an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days. That period has very likely run since 22 September. A failure to assess or notify is itself a compliance issue.
- **Expanded penalty and enforcement regime:** the Privacy Act regime has been strengthened.
- **New statutory tort:** a statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy now applies.
- **Customer contract exposure:** this includes potential exposure under the Bluefen contract.

**Push back:**
- **Information rights now:** the incident date, the forensic report, access logs, and the Company's documented eligible data breach assessment. If the OAIC or individuals were notified, we need copies of those notifications.
- **Pre-Completion covenant:** the Company must complete the investigation and make any required notifications, in consultation with the Buyer.
- **Specific indemnity** for all Losses arising from the incident, including:
  - regulator costs and penalties, where they are lawfully indemnifiable;
  - claims by individuals;
  - customer claims and credits;
  - remediation costs.
  The indemnity should be outside the cap, basket and knowledge or disclosure exclusions, with survival of at least 3–4 years, and supported by escrow.
- **Warranties:** privacy and data security compliance, and no other incidents.
- **Insurance:** check whether the incident has been notified to the Company's cyber insurer, and if not, require it.
- **Delete** any characterisation of the matter as "not material" from the SPA and schedules.

### 12. Sandbar supplier renewals: 3 × AUD 110,000 (medium–high)
**Facts (Disclosure Letter item 8):**
- There are three "related" renewals totalling AUD 330,000.
- The Seller's own disclosure says to "read together for timing/scope."
- It is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Concern:** The pattern suggests a single commitment split into three parts, possibly to sit under:
- an approval threshold in the conduct-of-business covenants;
- a delegated authority limit;
- the de minimis.
The word "related" also raises a possible related-party question.

**Push back:**
- **Obtain the contracts (DD-008, DD-011)** and establish:
  - signing dates, and whether they were signed in the interim period;
  - the counterparty's identity and any relationship to Harbourglass;
  - term, termination rights and prepayment;
  - whether the value is accrued in the accounts.
- If the renewals are not ordinary course, require the Seller to either:
  - procure their termination or reduction pre-Completion; or
  - bear them through a price deduction or specific indemnity.
- Aggregation language in the de minimis (item 3) should capture series contracts.
- The conduct-of-business covenants should aggregate related or series contracts for the purpose of approval thresholds.

### 13. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) (medium)
The Seller's characterisations ("not a consent requirement"; "not triggered by share sale") are **not** warranted, and should not be relied on without our own review.

- **Lease:** Review DD-007 ourselves for deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording. Make the landlord notification a Completion deliverable, or a covenant with evidence of delivery. Add a warranty that no landlord consent is required.
- **Mossvale:** Check DD-009 for any definition of "assignment" that captures a change in control or a change in beneficial ownership. If it is ambiguous, seek a comfort or waiver letter pre-Completion.

## Part C: Security for claims

Harbourglass is a venture vehicle, so it may distribute the sale proceeds quickly. Even good contractual rights may then be hard to enforce. We should seek:
- **a general escrow or retention** of ~10% of the price for the general warranty survival period;
- **specific escrows** for:
  - Ironquay, until the assignment is delivered;
  - DD-006, until the investigation closes and the notification position is settled;
  - Bluefen, if Completion proceeds without full comfort.
- **a parent or fund guarantee**, if the escrow is not agreed.

**W&I note:** If W&I insurance is contemplated, known matters (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar) will be excluded from cover. They therefore need Seller-backed specific indemnities and escrow regardless.
